research.abstract: Long COVID (LC) affects millions of individuals worldwide, particularly those with preexisting comorbidities. However, when assessing comorbidity-related risk factors for LC, it remains unclear whether preexisting comorbidities should be defined prior to SARS-CoV-2 infection or LC diagnosis. This methodological choice may substantially bias estimates of LC risk. In this study, leveraging Electronic Health Records (EHR) from 6,130,413 adults with documented COVID-19 across 49 U.S. states in the National Clinical Cohort Collaborative (N3C) from 2020 to 2024, we evaluated the impact of different comorbidity exposure-window definitions on LC risk estimates. We developed ensemble cross-fitted double/debiased machine learning to adjust for individual- and county- level confounders. We found that defining comorbidities before infection rather than before LC diagnosis yielded 8%-314% higher adjusted attributable risks and 3%-34% higher adjusted relative risks across 16 major comorbidities. Comorbidity-associated risks generally declined from 2020 to 2024, while substantial demographic, socioeconomic, geographic, and multimorbidity-related disparities persisted. Exposure-window specification can be a major source of bias in estimates of LC risk, particularly for comorbidities prone to delayed clinical recognition or underascertainment. More broadly, our results highlight how temporal misclassification of exposures in longitudinal EHR studies can distort risk attribution and population-level inference for risk stratification for LC and prioritization of prevention strategies in clinical medicine and public health, respectively.

research.abstract: Master sex-determining genes (MSDGs) occupy the top of developmental hierarchies and act as molecular switches that initiate female or male differentiation. Despite their essential roles, MSDGs exhibit rapid evolutionary turnover across vertebrates. In this review, we examine the molecular evolutionary trajectories of three independently evolved vertebrate MSDGs-Sry in mammals, dmy in medaka fishes, and dm-W in Xenopus frogs-and assess the extent to which their evolutionary histories are consistent with initial functional innovation followed by relaxed functional constraint, possible tolerated functional decline, and potential replacement or loss. Regulatory rewiring, structural innovation, or key amino acid substitutions can generate a functional "Jump" that enables a newly arisen gene to cross the threshold required for sex determination and become established as a master regulator. Once the new sex-determining system is established, further increases in MSDG activity may provide little additional fitness advantage, allowing purifying selection to relax. Nearly neutral or mildly deleterious substitutions can then accumulate while residual activity remains sufficient for normal sex determination, producing a tolerated functional "Decline." Importantly, replacement need not await a decline in ancestral MSDG activity below the functional threshold. A newly emerging MSDG may become established through competition within a population while the ancestral determinant still retains sufficient sex-determining activity, thereby rendering the ancestral MSDG dispensable and permitting its subsequent functional decay or loss. Together, these cases suggest that the switch-like, threshold-dependent architecture of sex determination can permit initial innovation followed by relaxed functional constraint and, in some lineages, turnover of upstream master regulators. We propose "Jump-Decline" evolution as a testable conceptual framework linking the birth, functional relaxation, and potential turnover of vertebrate MSDGs.

research.abstract: Background: Codon usage bias has been analyzed in the Coffea arabica L. nuclear genome, yet comprehensive genomic resources for this species remain limited. The chloroplast genome, characterized by its maternal inheritance and high conservation, represents a valuable resource for investigating plant phylogeny, crop domestication, and maternal lineage evolution. Results: We assembled complete chloroplast genomes for 52 C. arabica accessions, encompassing four cultivars (Geisha, Catimor, Bourbon, and Caturra), four improved breeding lines within the Geisha group (Yunka No. 3, Yunka No. 4, G02, and G13), two Catimor breeding lines (CCCA25 and T5175), and four accessions of unknown cultivar origin. Comparative genomics, unrooted phylogenetic reconstruction (neighbor-joining and maximum likelihood), haplotype inference, and exploratory principal component analysis (PCA) were integrated to characterize the genetic architecture of these chloroplast genomes. These genomes ranged from 155,133 bp to 155,192 bp in length, displayed the typical quadripartite architecture, and exhibited GC contents of 37.43-37.44%. Gene annotation identified 131 genes, comprising 86 protein-coding genes, 37 tRNAs, and 8 rRNAs. Codon usage analysis revealed a pronounced bias toward A or U at the third codon position. We detected 194 SSR loci per plastome, among which mononucleotide A/T repeats predominated. Neighbor-joining and maximum-likelihood phylogenies, PCA, and haplotype network reconstruction consistently resolved the 52 accessions into three genetic clusters (C1-C3; C1 represented by a single divergent accession) and five distinct haplotypes. SNP and InDel profiling further showed that intergenic spacer (IGS) regions harbored the highest density of genetic variation. Conclusions: These genomes provide resources for germplasm characterization, phylogenetic studies, and marker-assisted breeding in coffee. They also establish a chloroplast-genome framework that, when integrated with nuclear genomics and expanded sampling, will help fully resolve the maternal history, domestication, and allopolyploid origin of Coffea arabica.

research.abstract: Background: Calcific aortic stenosis (AS) is one of the most common and prognostically relevant valvular heart diseases, with a growing global burden driven by population ageing. Prediction of disease progression from moderate to severe AS, which would be instrumental for earlier diagnosis and treatment, remains challenging. At the same time, moderate AS is increasingly recognized as a heterogeneous condition associated with clinically relevant risk, particularly in patients with cardiac damage, heart failure, or rapid disease progression. Conventional echocardiographic parameters incompletely capture the biological heterogeneity underlying AS progression. The MODAS study was established to investigate biomarkers and mechanisms of AS progression and outcome using longitudinal multimodal phenotyping. Methods: The MODAS Study is a prospective, multicenter, longitudinal observational cohort study enrolling adults with moderate calcific tricuspid AS at three tertiary heart valve centers in Germany. Participants undergo standardized baseline assessment including clinical phenotyping, laboratory testing, electrocardiography, transthoracic echocardiography, cardiac computed tomography and cardiac magnetic resonance imaging. Biospecimens are collected for biomarker, immunologic, proteomic, and genetic analyses, including genome-wide association studies and assessment of clonal haematopoiesis. Participants are followed annually for up to 5 years with repeat clinical assessment, laboratory testing, and echocardiography. The primary endpoint is time to progression to severe AS according to 2025 ESC/EACTS guideline criteria or aortic valve replacement for severe AS, adjudicated by the local multidisciplinary Heart Team. Secondary endpoints include all-cause mortality and additional clinical outcome trajectories. Multimodal data integration will be used to develop and validate prediction models for disease progression and outcome. Discussion: The MODAS Study will provide a harmonized, deeply phenotyped longitudinal dataset to improve risk stratification in moderate AS and to identify imaging, inflammatory, and genetic markers associated with rapid progression and adverse outcomes. The study is designed to support future personalized surveillance strategies, improved selection for earlier intervention, and mechanistic understanding of calcific AS progression. Trial registration: ClinicalTrials.gov NCT05851209 . Registered on 9 May 2023.

research.abstract: Background: The CMS GLP-1 Bridge demonstration (July 2026-December 2027) expands access to GLP-1s for additional eligible Medicare Part D beneficiaries for a $50 monthly copay. Its long-run value depends on uptake, discontinuation, and which beneficiaries initiate therapy, in addition to policy decisions. Methods: We used the Future Elderly Model, a microsimulation of Americans aged 55 and older, to model the costs and benefits of expanded GLP-1 access to the newly Bridge-eligible population, assuming that it continues over a 10-year horizon and is accompanied by reduced GLP-1 pricing taking effect for already covered indications in Part D beginning in 2028. We compared a status quo with two expanded-access scenarios: high discontinuation paired with high reinitiation (Rodriguez et al.), and low discontinuation paired with low reinitiation (Understanding America Study). Each scenario was run for two different definitions of the Bridge-eligible population - a broad definition that includes beneficiaries with prior myocardial infarction or stroke and a narrow definition that excludes them. Results: Expanded access generated positive net social value in every scenario, from $44.3 billion to $58.5 billion over 10 years. Medicare net spending fell in every scenario, with cumulative savings of $21.2 - 27.1 billion, including $31.9 billion in diabetes drug price savings. Return on investment was 117 - 216% for Medicare and 198 - 346% for society. The eligible population mattered more than persistence. Net social value was 23 - 29% higher in the narrow population, because its initiators are healthier and have more to gain form access to GLP-1 treatment. Low discontinuation raised net social value by only 2 - 7% but raised Medicare drug spending, so ROI was higher under high discontinuation. Conclusions: Expanded Medicare access to GLP-1s is projected to produce substantial social value across a range of persistence and eligibility assumptions. Extending the lower demonstration price to previously covered indications would allow the program to pay for itself from Medicare's perspective. Because health gains accrue over many years, evaluating the demonstration only over its 18-month window would understate its benefits.

research.abstract: Background. Myocardial infarction (MI) outcomes depend on time to treatment, and fatigue and sleep disturbance are often reported in the weeks before the event. Whether wearable-measured sleep changes within individuals before MI, and whether such change is specific to MI, is unknown. Methods. In the All of Us Research Program, adults with a first MI code and at least 180 valid Fitbit sleep nights in the preceding 360 days were matched to up to 10 controls on sex, comorbidities, sleep apnea, calendar time and a propensity score. The full matched cohort of all cases was the primary cohort, and cases with diabetes and/or hypertension formed a subgroup. The main endpoints were the within-person change in night-to-night variability (SD, RMSSD, CV) of the REM-sleep fraction at days 30-16 relative to each persons baseline (days 360-121) and from days 30-16 to days 15-1, tested against 10,000 randomly placed index dates with allowance for the choice of window (max-T). The same pipeline was applied to cases without recorded symptoms or treatment, to an index date at the first angina code, to a cohort including heart failure and to ischaemic stroke and admissions for heart failure, pneumonia, fracture or appendicitis and any cause, and the analysis was adjusted for nightly heart rate, wear and device. Results. The full matched cohort comprised 45 cases and 450 controls. REM-fraction variability changed transiently before MI, decreasing at days 30-16 and returning towards baseline over days 15-1; allowing for the choice of window, this decrease-then-return pattern was rarely matched at 10,000 randomly placed index dates (max-T p<0.001). Its components were the decrease in SD at days 30-16 (Cliffs {delta} -0.30, p=0.004; OR per SD 0.53, 95% CI 0.35-0.80; max-T p=0.0034) and the return in RMSSD over days 15-1 ({delta} +0.36, p<0.001; max-T p=0.0035); day by day, the decrease was not detected as a continuous change (cluster permutation test p=0.58). The decrease in SD was not seen at the same time before admissions for pneumonia (69 cases), fracture or appendicitis (130) or any cause (859) and was larger before MI than before each of them (difference in {delta} -0.25 to -0.34), whereas the rise over days 15-1 was shared with pneumonia; it was of similar size in the subgroup with diabetes and/or hypertension, in cases without recorded symptoms or treatment, with the index date at the first angina code, when people with heart failure were included and after adjustment for nightly heart rate, wear and device. Scoring each person against their own baseline discriminated cases from controls with AUCs of up to 0.66, probably an optimistic estimate because the decrease in RMSSD was attenuated in held-out halves of the matched sets. Conclusions. In adults who use consumer wearables, a first MI was preceded by a transient change in night-to-night REM-sleep variability, a decrease at days 30-16 and a return over the following two weeks. The decrease was not seen at the same time before other acute admissions, did not depend on recorded symptoms or treatment and was detectable against each persons own baseline with simple measures. The timing is an exploratory finding, to be confirmed in new cases.

research.abstract: Background Effective type 2 diabetes (T2D) education improves patient outcomes, but clinician time constraints limit what can be covered during encounters. Large language models (LLMs) offer a scalable way to answer patient questions, yet their accuracy and reliability in T2D education across health literacy levels remain poorly characterized. Methods We developed DiaBench, a standardized benchmarking framework built from 96 question-and-answer pairs collected by clinicians from representative real-world patient encounters. GPT-5 transformed each pair into multiple-choice questions (MCQs) under three configurations (1-3) simulating different question formats and levels of user background. A five-member panel of certified diabetes care and education specialists (CDCESs), medical doctors (MDs), and endocrinologists validated the transformations, rating question rephrasing, answer rephrasing, and answer correctness. We then evaluated seven LLMs (GPT-51, Gemini-2.5-Flash2, Cohere Command3, Llama-44, DeepSeek-R15, Perplexity Sonar6, Mistral-Large-2.07) for accuracy and self-consistency across three runs. Results (i) Expert validation showed a consensus over MCQ transformation. For configuration 1, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of rephrased answers were appropriate, 98.1% (SD 0.01) of MCQ answers were correct, and 95.0% (SD 0.05) of rephrased questions were appropriate; corresponding values for configuration 2 were 96.3% (SD 0.05), 97.5% (SD 0.02), and 89.8% (SD 0.14). (ii) across benchmarking for configurations 1 and 2, most models achieved high accuracy ([≥]95%), but Mistral-Large-2.0, Llama 4, and Perplexity Sonar showed substantially lower self-consistency (60.4%-91.7%) than other models ([≥]95%). All models degraded in both accuracy and self-consistency on configuration 3. Conclusions DiaBench quantitatively differentiates LLM capability in T2D patient education, with Gemini, GPT-5, and DeepSeek-R1 performing strongly and other models suboptimally. DiaBench provides a transferable platform for evaluating existing and newly developed LLMs, addressing the need for standardized benchmarking before clinical deployment of LLM-based systems in patient education.

research.abstract: BACKGROUND: Lineage 8 (L8) occupies a unique phylogenetic position as a sister clade to all other known Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex (MTBC) lineages. Although the initial identification of L8 strains was limited to Rwanda and Uganda, the complete geographical distribution of this lineage remains undetermined due to limited genomic surveillance across eastern and central Africa. METHODS: We performed whole genome sequencing (WGS) on MTBC isolates from rifampicin-resistant tuberculosis (TB) patients' sputum in Bukavu, South Kivu province, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Lineage assignment was performed using TBProfiler with classification based on single nucleotide polymporphisms (SNPs). Phylogenetic reconstruction was conducted using maximum likelihood analysis against publicly available L8 reference genomes from Rwanda and Uganda. Drug-resistance profiles were determined through both genotypic prediction from WGS data and phenotypic drug-susceptibility testing. Clinical and epidemiologic data were extracted from programmatic records. RESULTS: We identified three clinical isolates belonging to MTBC L8 among fifteen sequenced isolates collected in Bukavu between January and December 2023 enriched for rifampicin resistant TB as determined by Xpert Ultra. Phylogenetic analysis confirmed placement within the L8 clade while revealing unique SNP profiles distinct from previously published Rwandan and Ugandan L8 strains by 16-20 to >200 SNPs, respectively, consistent with local diversification rather than recent cross-border importation. Ancestral genomic features characteristic of L8 were preserved, including the intact cobF region and complete pks8 gene. Drug-resistance prediction from genomic data indicated multidrug-resistant and pre-extensively-resistant TB. CONCLUSIONS: This report extends the known geographic distribution of MTBC L8 to eastern DRC, supporting the hypothesis that the African Great Lakes region harbors under-characterized ancestral diversity of the tubercle bacillus. Systematic genomic surveillance across the DRC-Uganda-Rwanda-Burundi corridor, including rifampicin-susceptible isolates, is needed to determine whether L8 represents a rare relict lineage or an under-detected endemic variant circulating through regional transmission networks.

research.abstract: Abstract Polygenic risk scores (PRSs) have improved substantially in predictive performance, yet results remain difficult to compare across studies that differ in cohorts, phenotype definitions, and evaluation procedures. Comparison to machine-learning methods is harder still, since their performance depends strongly on how data are partitioned and whether related individuals leak across splits. Here, we introduce a family-aware benchmark for polygenic prediction built on version 9 of the All of Us Research Program (AoU). The benchmark assigns entire family components to fixed discovery, calibration, and test partitions, reserves first-degree relatives for within-family evaluation, and separates models trained only on AoU discovery data from those using external GWAS summary statistics. This enables direct comparison between conventional PRS pipelines and machine-learning models trained under identical data budgets. We report results for 14 binary disease traits. Our strongest scores explain 5.7–24.9% of liability-scale variance, with particularly strong prediction for Alzheimer’s disease, type 2 diabetes, prostate cancer, glaucoma, and inflammatory bowel disease, and match or exceed published commercial and academic scores for most traits. Across 12 traits with interpretable within-family estimates of within-sibship-to-population effect ratio, 11 confidence intervals included a ratio of 1. Type 2 diabetes showed an attenuation ratio of 0.86 [0.76, 0.97].

research.abstract: Deep learning sequence to function models can predict the molecular effects of genetic variants, but their predictions are limited to the cell types and assays they are trained on. Here we describe DNACipher, a deep learning model that predicts the effects of genetic variants across diverse biological contexts-including those not directly measured. DNACipher takes 524 kb of genome sequence as input and predicts variant effects across 38,582 cell type/assay combinations, > 6 times as many contexts as AlphaGenome. We also introduce DNACipher Deep Variant Impact Mapping, a method to prioritize variants within trait-associated loci based on elevated predicted molecular effects relative to non-trait-associated variants. Applied to 590,604 common and rare variants at GWAS loci across 10 complex traits, DVIM identified imVars at > 90% of GWAS loci for 9 out of 10 traits. Common imVars were significantly concordant with statistical fine-mapping, and rare imVars were enriched for prior trait associations. For type 1 diabetes (T1D), imVars also had predicted effects that were supported by single-nucleus ATAC-seq, luciferase assays, and massively parallel reporter assays. DNACipher DVIM prioritises common and rare variants at GWAS loci by predicting molecular effects across cellular contexts.

research.abstract: Abstract Salticidae (jumping spiders) is the most species‐rich family within Araneae. Despite recent advances in phylogenomic studies, mitochondrial genome (mitogenome) evolution and its contribution to understanding phylogenetic relationships in Salticidae remain poorly characterized. Here, we present a mitochondrial phylogenomic analysis of 107 salticid species representing all seven recognized subfamilies. Using newly generated and publicly available mitogenomes, we investigated phylogenetic relationships and evolutionary patterns across the family, with a particular focus on comparisons between the highly diverse Salticinae and the species‐poor non‐Salticinae lineages. Our results show that the salticid mitogenomes are highly conserved in overall structure, with broadly similar genome size and nucleotide composition between Salticinae and non‐Salticinae lineages. Codon usage showed a pronounced A/T bias, with both mutational pressure and natural selection contributing to codon usage patterns. Phylogenetic analyses strongly supported the monophyly of Salticidae and all seven subfamilies in the maximum likelihood and Bayesian analyses. Lyssomaninae and Asemoneinae were recovered as sister groups, as were Eupoinae and Spartaeinae, while Onomastinae was sister to the clade comprising Hisponinae and Salticinae. Within Salticinae, Amycoida and Salticoida were recovered as major lineages, although relationships within Salticoida were unstable among analytical methods. Selection analyses indicated that all 13 mitochondrial protein‐coding genes are predominantly under purifying selection, whereas nad2 showed the most consistent signals of positive selection in Salticinae across the branch‐site, FEL and MEME analyses. Fifteen distinct gene rearrangement patterns were identified in Salticidae, including 13 novel patterns, with M5 inferred as the gene order of the most recent common ancestor of Salticidae. Gene rearrangements were more diverse in non‐Salticinae, particularly within Spartaeinae. Transposition was inferred as the predominant type of mitochondrial gene rearrangements in Salticidae. Overall, this study provides mitochondrial evidence for phylogenetic relationships within Salticidae and contributes to our understanding of mitochondrial sequence evolution, selection and gene order evolution in jumping spiders.

research.abstract: Abstract Context Approximately 80% of tuberculosis (TB) disease in the United States arises from untreated latent TB infection (LTBI). Primary care clinics are well positioned to address LTBI in populations disproportionately affected by TB, yet implementation barriers remain poorly characterized. Objective Identify barriers and facilitators encountered during early implementation of a multidisciplinary LTBI case management intervention (CMI) in a federally qualified health center (FQHC) serving predominantly non-U.S.–born patients. Design Qualitative study using structured key informant interviews, analyzed with iterative thematic analysis. Staff and patients were conveniently sampled; patients were limited to those who completed treatment. Setting and Participants Three clinics within a FQHC in Seattle, Washington. Thirty-seven interviews were conducted (32 staff, 5 patients) from February 2023-May 2024. Main Outcome Measures Staff- and patient-reported barriers and facilitators to CMI implementation. Results Staff identified three barriers: 1) adapting to a new workflow, including technical challenges and role ambiguity; 2) clinic capacity and resource constraints, including staffing and limited language support; and 3) gaps in LTBI care, particularly chest radiograph access and patient questions after a positive test. Staff reported three facilitators: 1) division of labor through role-shifting, enabling detection of side effects and dosing errors; 2) standardized communication tools and educational materials improving consistency and staff confidence; and 3) collaboration via electronic messaging and structured meetings supporting iterative improvement. Patients mostly reported facilitators only, citing the proactive follow-up as central to treatment completion. Both groups cited the drug shortage as a barrier to treatment completion. Conclusions Multidisciplinary case management revealed facilitators and barriers in delivering coordinated care. Staff identified division of labor, standardized tools, and structured communication key to care coordination while patients emphasized staff encouragement and pro-active follow-up as central to treatment completion. Workflow integration, resource capacity, and post-diagnosis patient support should be considered when implementing or scaling similar models.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Enterovirus D68 (EV-D68) has predominantly caused infections in children, and detected cases have mainly been infected by subclade B3. In 2025, however, a substantial number of infections in adults was noted. Aim To detail the molecular epidemiology of the 2025 season in Europe. Methods Case and sequencing data was collected from members in the European Non-Polio Enterovirus Network (ENPEN). The participating sites included both clinical and public health laboratories. Results Data was collected from 13 countries at 23 sites. There were 187 clinical cases infected with EV-D68 and 127 detections in wastewater. Age data were available for 76% (143/187), among which 90 cases were adults. VP1-based genotyping showed subclade A2/D to predominate in all age groups and across all participating countries, as well as in the sewage sampling performed at one site. Two interclade recombinant sequences were detected among 22 whole genome sequences. Conclusion The observed shift towards adult cases and subclade A2/D predominance warrants continued monitoring to determine whether this represents a sustained epidemiological change. The detection of interclade recombinant variants highlights a need to supplement regular VP1-based genotyping with whole-genome sequencing.

research.abstract: Abstract Background We asked what topological structure adds to a clinical prediction model and how that addition should be measured. Drug-resistant tuberculosis (DR-TB) treatment outcome prediction is the testbed. The contribution is an evaluation design and a bounded null result. Methods Cross-sectional records for 9210 patients from the NIAID TB Portals programme were collated to one row per patient by worst-case aggregation, giving a 99-feature clinical schema. We derived two topological representations. A Mapper graph, built on a UMAP lens over a Gower dissimilarity, supplied four neighbourhood-position features. Local Vietoris–Rips persistent homology on each patient’s 26-point neighbourhood supplied degree-0 and degree-1 summaries, vectorised by the best of thirteen catalogued methods. We compared five feature configurations across four classifiers in a pipeline in which every topological step is fitted inside the training partition. A sealed test lockbox of 1776 patients, 463 of them with adverse outcomes, was opened once. We compared discrimination by the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) using paired DeLong tests with Bonferroni correction (corrected threshold 0.0125). Results No topologically augmented configuration meaningfully improved lockbox AUROC over the clinical-only baseline under any classifier. The best AUROC was 0.7548, achieved by the baseline with XGBoost. Across all sixteen comparisons the upper 95% confidence limit never exceeded +0.014 AUROC. Five comparisons met the corrected threshold. Four favoured the baseline, and one, under the support vector machine, favoured the augmented model by a negligible +0.0005 AUROC. The same features supported neighbourhood-based risk stratification and revealed variation in adverse-outcome composition across patient neighbourhoods: adverse-outcome purity ranged from 5.9% to 30.5% across the fifteen largest Mapper nodes, stably under resampling. Conclusions The findings support a complementary framing of topological data analysis in clinical prediction. Topological features are best understood not as replacements for clinical predictors but as an analytical lens that reveals geometric structure in the patient population not captured by the clinical feature representation alone.

research.abstract: Aims/hypothesis: To evaluate the effectiveness of a personalised intervention program aimed at improving medication adherence in people with type 2 diabetes who are non-adherent to oral diabetes and/or hypertension medication, compared to usual care including access to a diabetes website, after a six-month follow-up. Methods: Parallel-group randomised controlled trial with six-month follow-up conducted in community pharmacies in the Netherlands and United Kingdom. People with type 2 diabetes, 35-75 years and non-adherent to oral diabetes and/or hypertension medication were recruited. The intervention group received the personalised intervention program and the control group received usual care and an informative diabetes website. The primary outcome was medication adherence measured by telephone pill count and secondary outcomes were self-reported medication adherence, systolic blood pressure and HbA1c level. Linear regression analysis and longitudinal mixed model analysis were performed to assess intervention effectiveness. Results: The study population comprised 68 participants, 66.2% men with a median age of 65.0 [Q1 to Q3 59.3 to 71.0] years. Linear regression analysis for the primary outcome medication adherence showed no significant effect of the intervention (B -0.014, 95% CI -0.17 to 0.14). In addition, no significant differences were found between the intervention and control group for self-reported medication adherence (OR 3.18, 95% CI 0.89 to 11.37) and systolic blood pressure (B -1.41, 95% CI -9.64 to 6.83). Finally, the intervention group did not show better HbA1c levels compared to the control group (B 0.68, 95% CI 0.44 to 0.92). Conclusions/interpretation: We did not observe a statistically significant difference, nor a clinically point estimate of difference, in medication adherence between the intervention and control group of a personalised intervention program aimed at improving medication adherence in people with type 2 diabetes who are non-adherent to oral diabetes and/or hypertension medication after six-months follow-up. We therefore do not recommend implementation of the intervention program in daily practice. Trial registry number: Registered in the Dutch Trial Register (Trial NL8747) and ISRCTN Registry ( ISRCTN36009809 ). Social media post: No effect of a personalised intervention program was observed on medication adherence in people with type 2 diabetes. Future studies should first focus on alternative recruitment methods for non-adherent people with type 2 diabetes, before the effectiveness of the intervention can be re-evaluated in a larger study sample. Keywords: Medication adherence, type 2 diabetes, intervention, pharmacy, effectiveness

research.abstract: Abstract Following the discovery of the piperazic acid (Piz)-containing hexapeptide demiguisin A from a toxic bird-associated Amycolatopsis strain, we aimed to investigate the structural diversity and bioactive potential of this natural product family. Here, we used the dmg biosynthetic gene cluster from Amycolatopsis sp. PS_44_ISF1 as a pathway mining probe to search for alternative demiguisin A producers. A global search identified only one other soil-derived Amycolatopsis sp. NBC_01488, encoding a highly syntenic pathway. Under feather-mimicking conditions, PS_44_ISF1 demonstrated enhanced growth and metabolite production relative to NBC_01488. Despite phylogenomic distance, both strains produced shared metabolites, while NBC_01488 yielded more abundant demiguisins, enabling the isolation of five novel derivatives characterized by two Piz-moieties with different hydroxylation patterns and glycine truncation. Two congeners displayed potent activity against the avian pathogen Mycobacterium intracellulare and moderate activity against Mycobacterium tuberculosis . These findings show that targeted pathway mining guided the expansion of the chemical diversity of Piz-modifications and demiguisin congeners with promising anti- Mycobacterium activity.

research.abstract: Background Misinformation decreases public confidence in health technologies and willingness to use them. Psychological inoculation, or "prebunking", exposes people to misleading claims before they spread widely and refutes the claims and embedded persuasion tactics. Evidence on its effectiveness for HIV-related misinformation, particularly in sub-Saharan Africa and among young women (a population highly vulnerable to HIV), is limited. Methods We conducted a randomised controlled trial (July to October 2025) among 2,163 women aged 18-29 years recruited online in South Africa. Participants were randomly assigned to view two short TikTok-style inoculation videos addressing common myths about an HIV vaccine, or attention-matched control videos on nutrition and diabetes. All participants then viewed multiple false claims presented as social media posts. The primary outcome was intention to receive an HIV vaccine if available (1-10 scale), assessed immediately post-intervention and at three-week follow-up. Secondary outcomes included likelihood of recommending the vaccine; and perceived credibility, emotional impact, and shareability of misinformation claims. We used linear regression models to estimate intervention effects. Results Misinformation exposure reduced vaccine intentions by 0.63 points in the control group, while intentions increased by 0.30 points in the intervention group. Controlling for covariates and baseline intentions, post-exposure vaccine intentions were 0.92 points higher in the intervention group (95% CI 0.78, 1.06; p<0.01), a 12% relative increase. Intervention participants were also more likely to recommend the vaccine (+0.74; 95% CI 0.61, 0.88; p<0.01). Inoculation reduced perceived credibility, emotional distress, and sharing intentions across all false claims. Effects persisted at three-week follow-up (vaccine intentions: +0.97; 95% CI 0.78, 1.17; p<0.01). Conclusion Brief, scalable psychological inoculation delivered via social-media-style videos protected young women's HIV vaccine intentions, with effects generalising to novel claims and persisting over three weeks. Prebunking campaigns may safeguard public confidence in other new HIV prevention technologies like lenacapavir.

research.abstract: Efficient evaluation of sequence data likelihoods and their high-dimensional gradients on phylogenetic trees improves inference under both maximum-likelihood and Bayesian frameworks. Here, we present BEAGLE 4.1, a high-performance library for statistical phylogenetics that incorporates new algorithms to evaluate these gradients on phylogenetic trees. We also provide new hardware implementations for both likelihoods and gradients supporting ARM NEON intrinsics and optimized matrix multiplication units -- called tensor cores -- on NVIDIA graphics processing units (GPUs). We benchmark the performance scaling of the library across a number of patterns and taxa on multi-core CPUs and GPUs, and compare the speedup afforded by NVIDIA and AMD GPUs as well as performance scaling with an increasing number of GPUs. We show that multi-core CPU implementations provide up to a fourfold speedup over single-threaded CPU implementations and up to an tenfold speedup for nucleotide and codon models, respectively, with performance generally improving as the number of taxa and site patterns increases. GPUs outperform multi-threaded CPU implementations for a realistic number of patterns, even for nucleotide models with a small state-space size of 4, while for codon models they provide substantially higher performance gains even for a single pattern or four taxa. Tensor cores on GPUs provide up to 2-fold speedup relative to standard CUDA cores for codon models. Using NEON instructions on ARM CPUs affords up to a $\sim 1.3$-fold speedup over non-SIMD implementation with the speedup going down to 1.1-fold at 8 CPU threads. We provide these new algorithms to evaluate the gradient and efficient hardware implementations for both likelihood and gradient calculations through BEAGLE 4.1, such that they can be readily integrated into phylogenetic software packages.

research.abstract: In 2023, an estimated 13% of worldwide deaths resulting from antimicrobial resistance (AMR) were due to drug-resistant TB (DR-TB). The World Health Organization (WHO) documented a dramatic, sixfold increase in the number of patients treated with 6-month all-oral (BPaLM) regimens, from 5,653 patients in 2023, to 34,000 patients by 2024, while also documenting an emergence of bedaquiline resistance in real-world cohorts and a lack of efficacy of BCG revaccination in the BCG-PRIME Phase 2b trial against sustained Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. Concurrently, the M72/AS01E subunit vaccine trial completed recruitment (approximately 20,000 individuals) across five high-burden countries, 11 months ahead of scheduled completion date. The first randomized controlled trial assessing DRTB-HDT host-directed therapy for DR-TB in adults (metformin + dovramilast), conducted at five international sites, is entering the late-stage readout phase. This synthesis of data, covering the period from 2015 through 2026, across six different dimensions includes molecular mechanisms of resistance, novel antimicrobial treatment modalities, host-directed therapy, immunity associated with regulatory compliance, adjuvants to vaccines, and the clinical translation of vaccine candidates. The Molecular-to-Translational continuum is used as a framework for the synthesis, with the regulatory immune function domain (T regulatory cells, myeloid-derived suppressor cells, and check-point axes) linking all five domains. Our central hypothesis is that drug resistance evolution of the microbe and failure of the host to maintain regulatory immunity are interdependent and create a bidirectional relationship with each other. We have identified nine major research gaps, with milestone dates from 2026 to 2030, based on unresolved controversies regarding the bedaquiline resistance catalog and the acquisition versus transmission narrative.

research.abstract: The increasing prevalence of drug-resistant Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) and nontuberculous mycobacteria (NTM) underscores the need for novel strategies. Mycobacteriophages are attracting growing interest for therapeutic and diagnostic applications. Here, we describe four new subcluster A3 phages (Cat, Goose1D, Goose1X, and Shep) and investigate their genomic diversity and lytic activity. The phages share >98% nucleotide identity with known A3 members but carry distinct deletions within the lysogeny module: Cat and Goose1X have different repressor-loss variants, and Goose1D lacks the integrase gene, whereas Shep retains an intact module. All phages lysed M. tuberculosis H37Rv, with efficiencies of plating (EOPs) of 10 -2 -10 -1, but showed limited activity against NTM. Cat was the most effective against drug-resistant Mtb isolates (EOPs of 10 -1 -1), remained stable across a broad pH and temperature range, but had a low burst size (8 PFU (plaque-forming units/cell). In lysogeny assays, 6% of Cat-exposed M. smegmatis colonies exhibited a lysogen-like phenotype, but no phage DNA was detected, suggesting spontaneous resistance. Sequencing of one strain revealed an H535Q substitution in the pyruvate carboxylase MSMEG_2412. These findings highlight lysogeny module plasticity in closely related phages and position Cat, with its naturally occurring repressor deletion and potent lytic activity, as a promising candidate against drug-resistant tuberculosis.

research.abstract: Polygenic risk scores (PRS) assume additive SNP effects, yet genetic risk also arises from interactions between loci and environmental factors that contribute to broad-sense heritability. We developed an extended PRS (ePRS) framework for type 2 diabetes (T2D) that incorporates locus-by-locus non-additive effects beyond those captured by additive single-locus PRS or linkage disequilibrium (LD) tagging. These were modelled as interaction-informed cumulative burden (G+G; summed allele counts), epistasis-screened (GxG; allele count products), and gene-environment effects derived from cardiometabolic variables in electronic health records. Across 235,000 UK Biobank participants, five complementary ePRS models captured largely non-overlapping high-risk individuals, suggesting that a key to individual risk predictions comprises the inclusion of multiple interaction-driven biological components rather than a single signal. A composite score was predictive over traditional additive PRS and predictive of T2D among individuals whose clinical symptoms fall within normal ranges.

research.abstract: Diabetes screening can alter both clinical care and patient behavior, but its consequences for health and socioeconomic outcomes remain uncertain. We examine these consequences in a fuzzy regression discontinuity design using electronic health records from the American Family Cohort (AFC) and longitudinal data from the Health and Retirement Survey (HRS). In AFC, we find that the diagnosis discontinuity peaks at 13 percentage points within six months and attenuates until it becomes insignificant at 42 months. We find a smaller and shorter-lived discontinuity for related prescriptions. These discontinuities remain across alternative specifications. Apart from specification and treatment window-dependent improvements in weight, BMI, and serum glucose, we do not observe a pattern of sustained improvement in cardiometabolic outcomes as a result of diagnosis and related care. In HRS, the threshold induces reductions of 22 percentage points in working for pay and 20.6 percentage points in labor-force participation at the two year follow-up. We do not observe a corresponding change in retirement, suggesting that diabetes diagnoses may lead to respondents reducing work without retirement. These reductions remain after several sensitivity checks but do not persist beyond two years. These findings suggest that health screening for chronic conditions may temporarily reduce labor supply, making employment responses relevant to the evaluation of broader costs and benefits of screening. research.abstract: Abstract Positive selection of somatic mutations is a driving force for cancer progression. Growing evidence shows that the emergence of a driver mutation in a tumor sample depends on individual-specific contexts, for example environmental exposures or the germline genetic background. Mutations in a driver gene could potentially bring different growth advantages in different contexts, resulting in differential selection of genes in varying contexts. Identifying which contexts modulate selection strength provides critical insights into the selection forces driving tumorigenesis. However, due to the sparsity of somatic mutations and heterogeneous background mutational process across positions and individuals, identification of differential selection has limited power with current statistical tools and is prone to false positives. To address this, we developed a powerful statistical method, DiffDriver, that identifies associations between contexts and selection strength of a driver gene across individuals. DiffDriver accounted for variations of mutation rates across bases and individuals, while taking advantage of functional information of sequences to improve power. In simulations, DiffDriver reduced false positives and boosted power compared to current methods. Multiple individual-level factors created significant heterogeneity in the strength of selection acting on driver genes: 24.3% of driver genes showed differential selection in at least one of the clinical traits studied, and 8.2% of genes had differential selection in different tumor immune subtypes. These results provide insights into the context-associated forces driving cancer evolution. Significance DiffDriver is a powerful statistical method that identifies associations between individual-level contexts and the strength of selection of driver genes, which revealed a substantial degree of differential selection of cancer genes.

research.abstract: Abstract Many patients living with chronic kidney disease (CKD) may not have a clearly identified cause, which can be a barrier to targeted therapies. We assessed the assignment of CKD etiologies in the national Veterans Health Administration (VHA) electronic health record data, overall and by demographics. We identified regular VHA users aged 18 - 100 years with new-onset CKD based on persistent eGFR <60 ml/min/1.73m 2 occurring 2005-2015. CKD etiologies were identified by administrative codes over 3 years before and after the incident CKD date. Etiologies were categorized as diabetic, hypertensive/vascular, obstructive/urologic, glomerular, cystic/congenital, and tubulointerstitial. CKD was considered recognized, but without etiology, if only a general CKD code was present. Logistic regression models assessed disparities by sex and race/ethnicity after adjustment for age, US Census region, and calendar year of incident CKD. Among 452,851 Veterans with CKD, 42.5% were assigned at least one etiology. Hypertensive/vascular (24.5%) was the most common. After adjustment, non-Hispanic Black Veterans and Hispanic Veterans were more likely to be assigned an etiologically-specific diagnosis than non-Hispanic White Veterans (OR 1.61 and 1.23, respectively, each p<0.001). Differences were greater at younger ages. Non-Hispanic Black Veterans were much more likely to be assigned a hypertensive/vascular etiology (OR 2.17; p<0.001), but both non-Hispanic Black and Hispanic Veterans were more likely than White veterans to be assigned diabetic and glomerular etiologies as well (each p<0.001). Women were much less likely to be assigned an etiology overall, and in all categories, compared to men (each p<0.001). Women were less likely to have CKD recognized even if etiology was not assigned. Overall, the assignment of an etiology for CKD is low among U.S. Veterans, particularly among women, possibly due to poor CKD recognition. Types of etiologies assigned differ by race/ethnicity, which may represent true etiologic difference or biased assignment.

research.abstract: Interdisciplinarity is an environmental state as well as an individual state. It refers to either a state of collaboration among individuals representing traditional academic fields or to a state in which an individual is proficient in how multiple fields think, communicate, and operate. In this work, interdisciplinarity is explored at the intersection of three academic fields: bioinformatics, chemistry, and HCI (Human-Computer Interaction). First, physicochemical property information is incorporated into codon substitution models at site-level resolution to provide a mechanistic understanding of how natural selection is constrained by such properties. Three PRIME (PRoperty-Informed Models of Evolution) models estimate the effects of property constraints--hydrophobicity, volume, electrical charge, alpha-helix propensity and beta-sheet propensity--at varying scopes. G-PRIME estimates the global effects of these five constraints across a sequence alignment, while E-PRIME captures episodic effects by estimating heterogeneity (K=2) within an alignment and then inferring property constraints for each class. S-PRIME estimates property constraints at each site in an alignment. The PREI (PRIME Imputation) method infers probabilities for 61 sense codon states at each site in an alignment based on S-PRIME, providing insights into how a site may evolve given evolutionary history and physicochemical constraints. PRIME models are compared with state-of-the-art methods such as CoRa (Conservation/Radical) and ESM-2 (Evolutionary Scale Modeling) using simulated and empirical datasets. Second, scientific communication for bioinformatics methods--specifically HyPhy (Hypothesis testing using Phylogenies), which models nucleotide sequence evolution--is investigated using concepts from HCI. The affordances of both traditional and GenAI (generative artificial intelligence) e-tutorials are examined across three studies. In Study 1, traditional e-tutorials from 22 representative bioinformatics software tools were collected and analyzed using quantitative and qualitative content analysis. These e-tutorials are not merely step-by-step guides: they are well-grounded, particularly in computer science, and serve as key resources for communication and collaboration. In Study 2, the potential of GenAI e-tutorials was explored through an autoethnographic approach. The autoethnographer identified how information-seeking behaviors with GenAI can be described using the conceptual frameworks of orienteering and information scent. In Study 3, information-seeking behaviors using traditional and retrieval-augmented GenAI (RAG) e-tutorials were compared under the orienteering framework. Data were collected from 10 participants through lab studies, surveys, and interviews. The exploring search state was observed only in the RAG e-tutorial group, likely due to an increased sense of latitude. Harnessing interdisciplinarity pushes the boundaries of scientific inquiry. The contributions of the work are methodological, empirical, artifact-based, and opinion-based. The holistic value of interdisciplinary research is evident, underscoring the further need for collaboration across fields and for improving such collaboration.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Zingiber emeiense Z. Y. Zhu is an endemic medicinal species restricted to Mount Emei in southwestern China. However, the lack of genomic resources has led to its frequent misclassification and has impeded evolutionary studies. Here, we assembled and characterized the first two complete chloroplast genomes (plastomes) of Z. emeiense . The two plastomes were identical in sequence and structure, each with a total length of 163,865 bp and exhibiting a typical quadripartite structure. Each plastome comprised a large single‐copy (LSC) region of 88,191 bp, a small single‐copy (SSC) region of 15,750 bp, and a pair of inverted repeats (IR) of 29,962 bp each. Each genome encoded 134 functional genes, including 86 protein‐coding genes, 40 tRNA genes, and eight rRNA genes, with an overall GC content of 36.04%. Comparative plastome analyses revealed that IR boundary variation and repeat sequence differences were major sources of genome size variation within Zingiber . Seven hypervariable regions ( psb M, trn T‐UGU, ycf 1, pet A‐ psb J, ndh F, psa C‐ ndh E, and rps 19) were identified as potential molecular markers. Likelihood‐based selection analyses revealed that plastid gene evolution was primarily driven by purifying selection, but ten genes showed signatures of positive selection; ycf 1, pet D, and rpl 2 exhibited lineage‐specific positive selection on the Z. emeiense clade. Phylogenomic reconstruction based on 70 complete plastomes placed Z. emeiense within sect. Cryptanthium , where it was strongly supported as a sister clade to Zingiber smilesianum and Zingiber teres . This study provides essential genomic resources for conservation and taxonomic studies of this endemic species.

research.abstract: ABSTRACT Understanding the minimal genetic changes underlying the earliest stages of speciation remains a central challenge in evolutionary biology. However, most model systems used to study early speciation involve pronounced ecological divergence, making it difficult to isolate the initial genetic changes associated with speciation. Here, we examined genetic differences between the cryptic cricket species Loxoblemmus campestris and L. sylvestris , which inhabit the same geographic region without pronounced ecological or morphological divergence. Despite their morphological similarity, the two species exhibited small but consistent molecular phylogenetic divergence in both mitochondrial and nuclear genomes. To investigate genetic divergence between these species, we conducted population genomic and comparative genomic analyses. We identified amino acid substitutions that were common within each species across orthologous genes and evaluated their evolutionary probabilities ( EP s) based on sequence conservation across Orthoptera. Although low EP amino acid substitutions occurred in multiple genes, three genes— Raf , Slit , and Sur‐8 —contained multiple such substitutions, and all three also showed elevated F ST values. These genes are functionally connected within the Ras/MAPK signaling pathway. These findings suggest that genetic divergence between L. campestris and L. sylvestris may involve changes concentrated in a limited number of functionally connected genes despite relatively few amino acid substitutions and limited phenotypic differentiation. Cryptic Loxoblemmus species may therefore provide useful systems for investigating early genomic divergence associated with speciation in the absence of pronounced phenotypic divergence.

research.abstract: Abstract Summary Bioinformatics analyses often rely on shell commands and small shell scripts whose executable context is difficult to preserve, inspect and reuse. TAFFISH addresses this gap by packaging command-line tool calls and lightweight shell flows as installable, versioned and inspectable executable units. Through a curated public Hub, TAFFISH indexes command interfaces, execution backends, platform constraints, release metadata and smoke-test/validation records. Together, these components provide a command-level reproducibility layer that works directly in ordinary shells and can also be invoked from existing workflow systems. Availability and Implementation TAFFISH is implemented in Common Lisp and released under Apache-2.0. TAFFISH version 0.10.1, together with the source code, documentation and public Hub resources, is available at https://github.com/taffish/taffish , https://taffish.com , https://taffish.github.io and https://github.com/taffish/ . The submitted software release, frozen Hub snapshot, test data, command logs, checksums and reproducibility package are archived at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21054185 . The authors will maintain the software and public resources for at least two years after publication. research.abstract: Abstract Humans exhibit a coevolutionary relationship between the trajectory of social evolution and senescence. A focal individual’s kinship network is a function of his/her life history, while that network in turn shapes the focal individual’s life history through kin effects on reproduction, generating a dynamic, nonlinear feedback loop across the population. Assessing directional selection on kin effects, therefore, requires explicitly modelling the feedback between the kinship network and life history. Here, we develop such a framework and apply it to examine selection pressures on the cooperative behaviour of closely related kin, including mothers, grandmothers, and older sisters. We hypothesise that the negative association of grandmothers, mothers, and older sisters ( > 10 years) with child mortality are under positive selection because increasing the absolute values of these kin effects would increase the stochastic growth rate. Furthermore, we hypothesise that the positive association of older sisters with child mortality is subject to negative selection, as increasing this effect would reduce the stochastic growth rate. We estimate kin-specific slope coefficients for child mortality using a Bayesian hierarchical model and solve a system of nonlinear equations linking kinship structure and survival to account for the nonlinear feedback between kinship and child survival. Thereafter, we compute stochastic sensitivities of both the stochastic growth rate and the mean lifetime reproductive output to these slope coefficients. Consistent with our hypotheses, all slope coefficients for kin presence on child mortality are negatively sensitive to both fitness metrics. We discuss the applications of our framework to examine the coevolution of social behaviours and senescence in age-structured populations. Highlight A time-varying nonlinear feedback model for the coevolution of life histories and kinship networks is presented. The model is valid for any age-structured population. The model enables sensitivity analysis of stochastic growth rate and lifetime reproductive output to kin effects on demographic rates. An application of the model to multiple countries at different stages of the demographic transition is presented.

research.abstract: Immunotherapies have shown limited efficacy in prostate cancer, largely due to its immunosuppressive tumour microenvironment. Hypersialylation contributes to immune evasion by engaging sialic acid-binding immunoglobulin-like lectins (Siglecs) on immune cells, forming glyco-immune checkpoints. Although this pathway represents a promising therapeutic target, the distribution of Siglec ligands across diverse prostate cancer phenotypes remains poorly understood. Here, we utilised high-affinity engineered sialoglycan-binding reagents (HYDRA) to perform immunohistochemical profiling of Siglec-7/9 ligands across a panel of 40 LuCaP patient-derived xenograft (PDX) models. Ligand expression was evaluated in relation to AR status and neuroendocrine phenotype. To determine the impact of androgen deprivation on the tumour glycome, ligand expression was compared between matched PDX lines grown in intact and castrated mice. Our findings reveal widespread but heterogeneous expression of Siglec-7/9 ligands across the LuCaP cohort. Expression levels were comparable between AR-positive adenocarcinoma models and AR-negative neuroendocrine variants, demonstrating that this glyco-immune checkpoint is maintained across distinct prostate cancer lineages. Under castration conditions, glycan remodelling occurred in a model-dependent manner. To evaluate these therapeutic dynamics in human disease, individual trajectory analysis of paired clinical specimens from the Movember GAP1-UTMA cohort was performed, revealing patient-specific responses that phenocopy the model-dependent glycan remodelling observed across the LuCaP lines. These findings support the sialoglycan-Siglec axis as a lineage-independent target and suggest that strategies aimed at disrupting Siglec-mediated immune suppression may be most effective when combined with androgen deprivation therapy to enhance anti-tumour immunity.

research.abstract: Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) caused disease Tuberculosis (TB) continues to be one of the leading causes of mortality although decades of medical research has progressed. With the alarming rise in multidrug-resistant and extensively drug-resistant strains, the effectiveness of conventional therapeutic regimens is being severely compromised. This mounting resistance not only diminishes the clinical success of existing drugs but also poses a significant health threat, underscoring the urgent need to develop innovative therapeutic strategies that can overcome resistance mechanisms and restore treatment efficacy. Recent research has revealed that Mtb relies on unique metabolic adaptations for its survival and persistence within the host, particularly through the shikimate pathway, the methylcitrate cycle and the glyoxylate shunt. These pathways enable the bacterium to synthesize essential metabolites, detoxify toxic intermediates and conserve carbon skeletons under nutrient deficient conditions. The enzymes involved in these pathways exhibit distinct structural and functional features that are absent in humans, making them highly selective as drug targets. Advances in structural biology, enzyme kinetics and computational approaches have facilitated the discovery of promising inhibitors derived from natural products, synthetic scaffolds and fragment-based designs. This review discusses the mechanistic insights, regulatory roles and inhibitor development efforts targeting key enzymes from these three metabolic pathways. By integrating biochemical, structural and medicinal chemistry perspectives, here in the potential of these metabolic nodes as underexploited yet powerful avenues for next-generation anti-tubercular drug discovery are reviewed.

research.abstract: Bacterial competence and genetic diversity are key determinants of microbial evolution, directly influencing pathogen adaptability, diagnostic reliability, and vaccine effectiveness. Natural transformation, together with horizontal gene transfer and homologous recombination, enables rapid genomic remodeling, facilitating the acquisition of antimicrobial resistance, modification of diagnostic targets, and generation of antigenic variants. These processes are particularly prominent in naturally competent and highly recombining pathogens, where population structures range from clonal to panmictic, shaping responses to selective pressures such as antibiotic use and immunization. This review synthesizes current understanding of the mechanisms governing bacterial competence and their role in generating genomic diversity, with emphasis on implications for diagnostics and vaccine design. Case studies-including Streptococcus pneumoniae, Neisseria meningitidis, and Helicobacter pylori-illustrate how recombination-driven diversification contributes to serotype replacement, diagnostic escape, and variable vaccine performance. Emerging approaches, including pan-genomic target selection, high-throughput sequencing, CRISPR-based diagnostics, and next-generation vaccine platforms, offer strategies to address these challenges but remain constrained by genomic variability and limited global surveillance. We argue that integrating evolutionary dynamics into diagnostic and vaccine development is essential for sustaining effectiveness. Continuous genomic monitoring and adaptive design frameworks will be critical to anticipate and mitigate competence-driven bacterial evolution in clinical and public health settings.

research.abstract: Abstract Despite being essential for fertility, many proteins involved in meiotic homologous recombination have diverged rapidly. The evolutionary forces driving this divergence remain mostly unknown, in part because of challenges in accounting for the interplay of sequence changes with constraints imposed by proteins’ structures and physiological roles. Here, we explore strategies to more sensitively detect signatures of positive or relaxed selection by integrating evolutionary analyses with structural and functional information, using meiotic recombination proteins in four taxa—primates, rodents, birds and budding yeasts. By mapping selection rate estimates onto predicted protein structures, we characterized protein regions likely to have experienced positive selection. We further identified subtle sequence variation within protein domains that are well conserved generally because of structural constraints. To detect sequence variation masked by these constraints, we analyzed selection at structurally matched residues, comparing homologs across different lineages as well as between meiosis-specific and generalist paralogs. These approaches identified lineage- and paralog-restricted enrichment of non-synonymous substitutions that may indicate loss of functional constraints and/or adaptive innovation. Finally, we used cross-species complementation experiments in Saccharomyces cerevisiae to show that sequence variation in the pro-crossover factor MSH4 modulates recombination proficiency. We suggest that evolutionary plasticity per se is a key conserved characteristic of the meiotic recombination machinery. More generally, our approach provides a mechanistic framework to analyze protein evolution. Significance Statement Meiotic recombination—the shuffling of genetic material during reproductive cell formation—is essential for fertility across all sexually reproducing organisms. Paradoxically, the proteins mediating recombination evolve rapidly despite their critical function. We used an integrative approach combining evolutionary analysis with protein structure prediction to understand how and why these proteins change. By mapping sequence variation onto protein structures and comparing meiosis-specific proteins to their generalist counterparts, we identified regions likely experiencing adaptive evolution or relaxed functional constraints. Experimental tests confirmed that sequence differences affect function. Our findings suggest that evolutionary plasticity itself may be a conserved feature of the recombination machinery. This structure-informed framework offers a generalizable strategy for detecting functionally relevant evolutionary changes in other protein systems.

research.abstract: Badnavirus decoloratiovitis , commonly known as Grapevine Roditis leaf discoloration‐associated virus (GRLDaV), is a member of the genus Badnavirus (family Caulimoviridae ) and a double‐stranded DNA pathogen associated with leaf discoloration symptoms in grapevine. In this study, the complete genome sequences and molecular characterization of two GRLDaV isolates, TR‐B42 and TR‐I3, obtained from grapevine varieties in Turkiye were determined. The complete genomes were amplified in nine overlapping fragments and assembled into circular double‐stranded DNA molecules of 7084 nt (TR‐B42) and 6987 nt (TR‐I3), with G + C contents of 41.2% and 41.5%, respectively. Both isolates exhibited the typical Badnavirus genome organization comprising four open reading frames (ORFs). Conserved domain analysis revealed a DUF1319 domain in ORF1 and characteristic Badnavirus replication domains, reverse transcriptase (RT), RNase H, zinc finger, and aspartic protease, within ORF3. Independent intrinsic‐disorder prediction of ORF3 across the six globally available GRLDaV isolates converged on a moderate‐to‐high disorder window localized to ORF3 amino acids ~830–890. This same interdomain window overlapped directly with the single prominent recombination hotspot detected in the TR‐B42 genome at nucleotides 3600–3800. Quantitative dN/dS analysis showed that ORF1‐3 were each under strong purifying selection, whereas ORF4 exhibited relaxed purifying selection. research.abstract: Abstract Plasmodium falciparum , the deadliest causative agent of malaria, harbours extensive structural variation that underlies key biological processes including drug resistance and diagnostic evasion. Here, we present PfPan, a P. falciparum pangenome constructed from 13 geographically diverse high-quality reference genomes using Minigraph-Cactus, adding 4.77 Mb of sequence beyond the 3D7 linear reference. We identify over 5,000 structural variants (SVs) across the reference genomes and demonstrate improved genotyping using the vg toolkit compared to linear reference-based approaches, with comparable performance for small variant discovery. Benchmarking against assembly-derived truth sets confirms pangenome superiority for structural variant detection, particularly at complex and hypervariable loci. Applying PfPan to 878 globally sampled P. falciparum whole-genome sequences, we characterise biologically and clinically relevant SVs, including the complex drug resistance-linked gch1 locus, and explore deletions upstream of the coding sequence for the diagnostic target HRP2. PfPan provides a foundational resource for mitigating reference bias in P. falciparum genomic surveillance and establishes a framework for improved detection of variants associated with drug resistance and malaria control in monoclonal P. falciparum samples that have not undergone selective whole-genome amplification.

research.abstract: Abstract: Benzothiazole (BTA), a fused bicyclic heterocycle of thiazole and benzene units, has become a special scaffold for medicinal chemistry with a vast pharmacological profile. Structural modification at the benzothiazole core provides enormous flexibility toward rationalizing bioactivity in a wide range of therapeutics. Contemporary research is exemplified by benzothiazole derivatives as potent antibacterial agents, efficiently targeting multidrug-resistant pathogens by mechanisms like DNA gyrase inhibition and membrane disruption. They also exhibit multi-target-directed ligand- based anti-Alzheimer's activity by inhibiting acetylcholinesterase, butyrylcholinesterase, monoamine oxidases, and β-secretase enzymes. In cancer, benzothiazole hybrids are found to be selectively cytotoxic toward different cancer cell lines, such as breast, lung, and liver cancers, and are generally more active than the traditional drugs. Anti-tubercular activity presents superior inhibition of Mycobacterium tuberculosis, including, Multidrug-Resistance (MDR) and Extensively Drug- Resistance (XDR), by novel hybrid conjugates and heterocyclic linkages. Additionally, benzothiazole analogues exhibit anti-inflammatory and anti-diabetic activity with cyclooxygenase, Dipeptidyl Peptidase-4 (DPP-4), α-glucosidase, and α-amylase enzyme inhibitory activity. Structure-Activity Relationship (SAR) analysis consistently indicates that electron-withdrawing or electron-donating functions, linker type, and heteroatom position in modulating pharmacological activity. Recent patents reflect sustained innovation in drug design with the benzothiazole motif, and therapeutic applications exist in antimicrobial, anticancer, neuroprotection, and metabolic disorders. Overall, these findings place emphasis on benzothiazole derivatives as highly effective lead templates with immense therapeutic value, warranting further consideration towards clinical usefulness.

research.abstract: Abstract Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a significant public health challenge, particularly among displaced populations. These environments foster TB transmission due to overcrowding, poor living conditions, and inadequate healthcare access Objectives To compare the proportion of tuberculosis (TB) cases detected through screening among displaced populations residing in internally displaced persons (IDP) and refugee settings with that among the general population in Benue State, Nigeria. Design Quantitative observational study comparing TB screening and diagnostic findings across displaced and general populations. Setting IDP camps, refugee settings and general-community screening locations in Benue State, Nigeria. Participants A total of 1,938 individuals were screened: 1,143 in displaced settings and 795 in the general population. Participants were assessed for presumptive TB and underwent the applicable diagnostic evaluation. Primary and secondary outcome measures The primary outcome was the proportion of screened individuals diagnosed with TB in displaced settings compared with the general population. Secondary outcomes were the numbers of presumptive TB cases and TB diagnoses classified as bacteriologically confirmed. Results Among the 1,143 individuals screened in displaced settings, 128 presumptive TB cases were identified, with 46 confirmed cases (26 bacteriologically and 20 clinically). In contrast, only 3 TB cases (2 bacteriologically and 1 clinically) were detected among 795 individuals in the general population. The TB prevalence rate in displaced populations was 4.0%, significantly higher than the 0.4% observed in the general population. Conclusions The study confirms a heightened TB burden in displaced communities, emphasizing the need for enhanced screening, diagnosis, and treatment strategies.

research.abstract: Background. Mycobacterium tuberculosis , the bacterium responsible for tuberculosis, remains a leading cause of global infectious disease deaths. While genomic epidemiology is essential for understanding transmission dynamics and the rise of antibiotic resistance, significant computational limitations currently prevent comprehensive phylogenetic analysis of the vast number of publicly available M. tuberculosis genomes. Methods. We developed UShER-TB, a comprehensive collection of community resources, including a computational analysis pipeline designed for scalable phylogenomic analysis of M. tuberculosis . To demonstrate this system’s utility, we processed 129,312 genomes to construct a global phylogeny. We evaluated the system’s accuracy in transmission cluster reconstruction, its ability to identify novel genetic lineages and its performance in placing ancient DNA samples within the global tree. Results. The pipeline successfully constructed a global phylogeny capturing genomic diversity from over 129,000 samples. UShER-TB achieved high accuracy in reconstructing transmission clusters, reaching an adjusted Rand index of 0.95 when compared to conventional phylogenomic methods. This tool also facilitated the identification of putative novel lineages and sublineages. Furthermore, the platform enabled the successful phylogenetic placement of ancient samples. The system allows for real-time analysis of new genomes to reveal transmission dynamics and introduction patterns on a global scale. Conclusions. This approach overcomes longstanding computational barriers in genomic surveillance. UShER-TB provides researchers with efficient tools for tuberculosis monitoring, particularly for resource-limited settings where the disease burden is highest. Trial registration. Not applicable.

research.abstract: Abstract The X chromosome carries an unusually high density of immune genes and is a major contributor to sex differences in immune function and autoimmune diseases. In females, X-chromosome inactivation (XCI) has two major functional consequences: it shapes X-linked gene dosage through XCI escape and determines the cellular exposure of heterozygous X-linked variants through XCI skew. Yet because XCI creates a mosaic of cells expressing different parental X chromosomes, these properties have remained largely inaccessible in individual women, becoming measurable only where XCI is non-random or after aggregation across large cohorts. Consequently, how X-linked variation contributes to sex-biased immunity and differs between individual women has remained unresolved. Here we present scDaisyChain, a graph-based framework that reconstructs chromosome-scale X haplotypes directly from heterozygous SNPs and single-cell long-read transcriptomes. scDaisyChain achieves near-ground-truth accuracy in highly polymorphic mouse hybrids and shows strong concordance with orthogonal long-read whole-genome phasing in human samples. Applied to peripheral blood immune cells from healthy women, it reveals a lineage-specific escape program in which lymphoid cells escape XCI more broadly than monocytes, with corresponding gains in the inactive X chromatin accessibility and female-biased expression. Lineage-specific skew further alters the proportion of cells expressing each heterozygous X-linked variant, a property we term variant exposure. Predicted deleterious variants are preferentially found in low-exposure states, exemplified by a splice-altering TLR8 variant expressed in few cytotoxic T cells. In rheumatoid arthritis (RA), the monocyte compartment - which has the lowest escape in health - shows reproducible inactive X dysregulation converging on a trained-immunity programme linked to disease flare and synovial macrophage activation, with elevated escape of IL13RA1 and HDAC8 . These findings establish lineage-specific escape, skew and variant exposure as quantifiable, patient-resolved determinants of sex-biased immune gene dosage and X-linked variant penetrance in health and autoimmune disease, resolving a dimension of female biology that has been previously inaccessible in individual donors. One Sentence Summary scDaisyChain resolves X-inactivation escape, skew and variant exposure in individual women, shaping immune dosage and autoimmune risk.
